steps.tx: **Systemic fungal infections** are invasive diseases caused by yeasts and moulds when host defences fail. Candida infects about 90% of immunocompromised intensive care patients, Aspergillus invades lungs in neutropenia under 500 cells per microlitre, and Cryptococcus causes meningitis in 15% of HIV patients with CD4 below 100. India reports near 50 cases of mucormycosis per one hundred thousand people in diabetic cohorts.
steps.say: Systemic fungal infections occur when host defences fail. Candida affects many intensive care patients who have lines and antibiotics. Aspergillus in this host invades lungs when neutrophil counts are very low. Cryptococcus causes meningitis in advanced hiv infection. Mucor is common in diabetics here.

steps.tx: **Risk factors** divide into neutrophil failure, T cell failure, and barrier breakdown. Prolonged neutropenia beyond 10 days, steroids above 3 weeks, central lines, broad antibiotics, and iron overload each raise invasive fungal risk. Uncontrolled diabetes with blood sugar above two hundred and fifty milligrams per decilitre predisposes to mucormycosis. About 40% of invasive aspergillosis occurs in non neutropenic intensive care patients, so the history of steroids matters as much as counts.
steps.say: Risk factors are neutrophil failure, t cell failure and barrier breakdown. Long neutropenia, prolonged steroids, lines and iron overload raise risk. Uncontrolled diabetes favours mucor. Many intensive care patients without low counts still develop aspergillus. Always check steroid use in every sick patient you review.

steps.tx: **Pathogenesis** starts with inhaled spores or colonising yeasts breaching epithelium. Macrophages digest spores, while neutrophils kill hyphae through oxidative burst. When these fail, hyphae invade vessels, cause thrombosis, and infarct tissue. Angioinvasion produces wedge shaped infarcts and easy spread across tissue planes. Candida instead forms biofilms on devices and sheds yeast into blood, producing microabscesses in kidney, liver, and brain.
steps.say: Fungi start as inhaled spores or colonising yeasts. Macrophages and neutrophils act to kill spores and hyphae in healthy hosts. When this fails hyphae invade vessels and cause clots. Invaded tissue infarcts and spreads. Candida forms films on devices and sheds yeast into the blood.

steps.tx: **Clinical features** are often subtle, so fever beyond 5 days without source in a neutropenic patient is never dismissed. Invasive aspergillosis gives pleuritic pain, haemoptysis, and cavitary nodules. Mucormycosis starts as facial pain disproportionate to signs, then black eschar on palate or nasal turbinates. Disseminated candidiasis shows hepatosplenic microabscesses with raised liver enzymes and eye involvement in 15% of cases.
steps.say: Fever beyond five days without a source in low counts is never ignored. Aspergillus gives chest pain, cough blood and cavitary nodules. Mucor starts with facial pain and then progresses to black dead tissue. Disseminated candida hits liver, spleen and eyes.

steps.tx: **Syndrome mapping** links organism to picture for quick recall. Rhizopus favours diabetic ketoacidosis with sinus and orbital spread. Cryptococcus favours headache with raised opening pressure and low blood sugar in spinal fluid. Histoplasma gives oral ulcers with adrenal failure mimicking Addison disease. Penicillium marneffei produces umbilicated papules on face in advanced HIV. Each syndrome points to one fungus before culture returns.
steps.say: Keep organism matched to picture for quick recall at the bedside. Rhizopus favours diabetic ketoacidosis with sinus and orbital spread. Cryptococcus gives headache with high pressure spinal fluid here. Histoplasma causes mouth ulcers with adrenal failure in many patients. Marneffei gives umbilicated face papules in patients with advanced hiv.

steps.tx: **First test** in suspected invasive mould disease is high resolution computed tomography showing nodule with halo sign or reversed halo sign, plus serum galactomannan above zero point five. The gold standard is tissue biopsy showing broad aseptate right angled hyphae in mucormycosis or septate acute angled hyphae in aspergillosis. Blood culture detects Candida in 70% but stays negative in most mould infections.
steps.say: Do high resolution scan for halo signs and serum galactomannan. The gold standard is biopsy showing hyphae shape. Blood culture finds candida often, but it stays negative in most mould infections.

steps.tx: **Antigen and antibody** tests refine diagnosis. Cryptococcal antigen in serum is positive in 95% of HIV meningitis cases and guides therapy. Beta D glucan above 80 picograms per millilitre supports invasive fungal disease generally but not the species. Histoplasma urine antigen helps in disseminated disease. Tissue culture with potassium hydroxide mount gives faster answers than culture alone and should be done in every suspected case.
steps.say: Antigen tests refine the diagnosis. Cryptococcal antigen is positive in most hiv meningitis cases. Beta d glucan supports fungal disease generally without naming species. Histoplasma antigen helps in disseminated disease. Always send tissue mount and culture in every suspected case you see.

steps.tx: **First line management** follows organism. Invasive aspergillosis gets voriconazole 6 milligrams per kilogram twice daily for 2 days then 4 milligrams per kilogram twice daily for at least 6 weeks. Mucormycosis gets liposomal amphotericin B 5 to 10 milligrams per kilogram daily with urgent surgical debridement. Fluconazole eight hundred milligrams daily is first line for cryptococcal meningitis after a week of amphotericin. Fluconazole four hundred milligrams daily suits mild candida bloodstream infection.
steps.say: Treatment follows the organism. Aspergillus therapy runs by weight for at least six weeks here. Mucor needs liposomal amphotericin with urgent surgery too. Meningitis therapy starts with amphotericin and then takes fluconazole. Mild candida bloodstream infection takes daily fluconazole for many days.

steps.tx: **Source control** matters as much as drugs. Remove central lines at once in candida bloodstream infection and repeat blood cultures every forty eight hours until clearance. Neutrophil recovery above 500 cells per microlitre improves aspergillus survival from below 20% to over 60%. Stop or taper steroids when safe. Echinocandins such as caspofungin 70 milligrams loading then 50 milligrams daily cover resistant Candida species in intensive care.
steps.say: Source control matters as much as drugs here. Remove lines at once in candida blood infection today. Recovery of neutrophils improves survival greatly for the patient too. Reduce steroids slowly when safe and possible for the patient. Echinocandins serve resistant candida species in intensive care.

steps.tx: **Complications and prognosis** include haemoptysis, bronchopleural fistula, orbital loss, and chronic cavitary aspergillosis with 5 year mortality near 50%. Invasive aspergillosis mortality is about 30% overall but above 80% in stem cell transplant recipients without neutrophil recovery. Disseminated candidiasis with endophthalmitis needs dilated eye exam within a week. Follow up scans at 4 to 6 weeks decide when to stop antifungals.
steps.say: Complications are cough blood, fistula, eye loss and chronic lung disease. Aspergillus mortality is about thirty percent overall and much higher without neutrophil recovery. Candida involves the eyes, so examine them within a week. Repeat scans decide stopping therapy.

steps.tx: **High-yield for the exam** locks hypha shapes, drugs, and timelines together. Mucor is broad and right angled without septa, Aspergillus is septate at 45 degrees. Candida bloodstream infection needs line removal and eye exam. Cryptococcal antigen is the rapid test, and galactomannan favours Aspergillus. Amphotericin nephrotoxicity is reduced in liposomal form, dosed at 3 to 10 milligrams per kilogram.
steps.say: Keep hypha shapes, drug choices and timelines together in mind. Mucor is broad and right angled while aspergillus is septate at forty five degrees. Candida needs line removal and eye exam. Liposomal amphotericin is safer on the kidney than conventional form.
